A.why: A clear tiered straw skirt of plates that flares, but wide cuffs square the shoulders and the shelf-like tiers stop short of the boots.

B.why: The prettiest and most on-brief skirt (long A-line of reed panels) with a good reed headpiece, let down by a belt bar that widens the waist and a boxy bodice.

C.why: The cleanest dress outline, a smooth cone skirt from a belted waist, but it reads as plain olive cloth with no armour and a crate-like coif.

D.why: A literal lamellar skirt, but a straight brown barrel under wide pauldron blocks that reads leather-family, not fen gown.

E.why: A stepped flare that ends in a floor-level plinth, all in one near-black green that loses every line at night.

F.why: No skirt to speak of: thigh-length plates over visible legs read as a soldier's tunic.

notes: Every set keeps wide square shoulder and sleeve blocks, so none reads as a narrow-shouldered woman from the high camera, and none combines a real flared skirt of plates with the fen palette and a pale trim; the best gown is still a step from store-page quality.
